description: issue #204 + issue #847: `clear_screen` clears the drawing and homes the turtle's position and heading to (0,0)/0 — and the homing is **observable**: it emits `move` (from [0 30], reporting the pre-reset heading 90) then `turn` (90 -> 0) before the single `clear{mode:"clear_screen"}`. Crucially there is NO `draw-segment` beside that `move` even though the pen is down, because the same instruction goes on to clear the drawing (spec/rendering.md:36's "a pen-down move appends one straight segment" describes what a move contributes to the RETAINED SCENE, and spec/rendering.md:148's "Clear operations" row fixes `clear_screen`'s contribution at *cleared*; escalated to the maintainer as issue #858) — the two events are independent, so "moved but drew nothing" needs no renderer special case. Before this fix the homing was silent, so a consumer replaying the stream believed the turtle was still at [0 30] heading 90 while the runtime reported the origin. spec/rendering.md:151 makes the `clear` PAYLOAD the minimum mechanism for reproducing the homing; these events are a deliberate, permitted superset that spares every consumer a `clear_screen`-shaped special case (animation, stepping, `why`, and `debug` already track position and heading through `move`/`turn` for every other turtle command), and under `tell` spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:113's identity requirement then applies to them directly. A following `forward` still draws from the origin at heading 0.
